if I follow @rsvoboda instructions, I have a NPE even in JVM mode.
I've identified the issue and I'll have a PR shortly

@geoand can you explain what you identified?

I see a lot of changes which look like refactoring to me, but I can not clearly see what actual root cause got solved. Was it CI or was it the testcases itself?

The basic problem was a change I had introduced regarding retrieval of the ObjectMapper.

CI was also sort of misconfigured due to the fact that the project was a multi module project

BTW, multi module was actually by design. Initially I ran into issues with stuff missing when building native. Back then I created a reproducer which I later modified into these test cases. So I wonder if changing it into single module will actually reproduce the original case.

I understand, but I am pretty sure that cases are being addressed now.
Furthermore I wanted this integration test to be similar to the others we have to keep things consistent.

It is good that you are confident, but I have my doubts. That tests still run fine is no guarantee that the actual code flow is exactly the same in case of single module. If I understood correctly in single module the Jackson annotated model classes will be indexed. In the multi module scenario they were not. So I wonder if the test scenario is still the same.

See #3652 for the original issue.

One could argue that we should take the same approach for modules we have, but we haven't so far :).

If an issue arises that requires that we specifically use a multi-module test, we can always reconsider.
My understanding of the original issue is that multi module was not the issue. So I think we will be fine.

Indeed multi module was not the issue itself, but quote from #3562 `Both the model and builder are in a separate (reusable) jar library`. How to reproduce this separate jar library in a test case without using multi module?

Sorry for being persistent, but I am just worried that future changes might break things unnoticed.

Also it is a pity to see README gone for which I got a 100  ([see here](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/3688#discussion_r319566660))

We can't of course guarantee that nothing will break, but we are pretty confident that the extension and the test cases are good (in large part due to your contributions).
Moreover from a maintenance perspective, having integration tests that are consistent across all extensions is a huge plus. 
The past month or so every time I looked at this integration test I was getting the feeling that it was a little odd due to module split. That coupled with the fact that the modules themselves didn't provide any apparent testing benefit (on the contrary they broke the scripts used to test all modules) led to me refactoring it.
